title: Bonami inequality in expectation form
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of degree at most $k$, meaning that every nonzero Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$ is supported on a set $S$ with $|S| \le k$. Writing $\E$ for the expectation under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$, we then have
\[
  \E[f^4] \;\le\; 9^{k}\,\bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n
f has degree at most k (every nonzero Fourier coefficient supported on a set of size at most k)
replaced:
The main Bonami inequality stated through the expectation operator: if a Boolean function $f$
has degree at most $k$, then
\[
\E[f^4] \le 9^{k}\,\bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^2.
